context: long-span roof gates MEP · crowd safety & broadcast drive commissioning

brief.intro: New to this project type? A stadium or arena is a long-span structural-steel roof with a seating bowl and a dense ring of concourse/back-of-house MEP hanging off it — so unlike a normal building, most of the MEP simply cannot start until the roof structure is up and safe to work under. The programme is really driven by two things that aren't structural at all: mass-egress crowd life-safety (voice evacuation, CCTV, access control) and the broadcast/AV/scoreboard infrastructure a modern venue is built around. Because the venue must move tens of thousands of people in and out safely within minutes, life-safety systems are commissioned to a much higher standard of proof than a typical commercial building — and that final proving, not the last piece of finish, is what usually determines the real handover date.

must_get_right: The long-span roof structure gates almost everything else — sequence its procurement and erection first and protect it as the critical-path driver.
Mass-egress life-safety (voice evacuation, exits, CCTV, access control) is commissioned and proven, not just installed — build in real time for it.
Broadcast/AV/scoreboard infrastructure is core scope now, not an add-on — coordinate its cabling and IT backbone with the main MEP rough-in, not after.
Plan an event-day systems rehearsal (all systems live, simulated crowd flow) before the first real event — it is the true final gate, separate from construction completion.

basis_of_planning.standard: AACE Recommended Practice 38R-06 — Documenting the Schedule Basis

sections.heading: Scheduling method & tools
sections.body: A Critical Path Method (CPM) network built in Primavera P6, developed to a Level 3 control schedule with retained-logic progress. The roof-steel package is modelled as its own sub-network given its scale and erection-sequencing risk.

sections.heading: Calendars & working time
sections.body: Civil and bowl structure run a 6-day week; roof-steel erection follows a crane-availability calendar with defined lift windows; MEP fit-out and commissioning move to extended hours ahead of the first event date.

sections.heading: Sequencing logic & critical path
sections.body: The driving path runs roof-steel procurement → erection → weather-tight envelope → MEP rough-in across bowl and concourse → life-safety and broadcast systems commissioning → event-day rehearsal. Most concourse and bowl MEP cannot meaningfully start overhead work until the roof structure is safe to work under.

sections.heading: Key assumptions
sections.body: Design freeze on seating capacity and life-safety egress strategy before structure proceeds; a fixed first-event date agreed with the client/operator; broadcast rights-holder requirements finalised before IT/AV rough-in; a single mobilisation.

sections.heading: Procurement & long-lead items
sections.body: The schedule is roof-steel-led. The following are tracked as milestones because they drive erection and fit-out sequencing:

sections.heading: Access, resource & site constraints
sections.body: Roof-steel erection needs dedicated large-crane windows and exclusion zones that limit other trades working below. Concourse and bowl MEP crews compete for access around the seating structure; broadcast/AV installation is coordinated with the rights-holder's own specialist contractors.

sections.heading: Risks, float & contingency
sections.body: Principal risks are roof-steel fabrication/erection slippage — which cascades into everything below it — and mass-egress re-test loops. Schedule contingency is held immediately before life-safety proving and before the event-day rehearsal rather than spread across finishing activities.

sections.heading: Schedule levels of detail
sections.body: Reported at Level 1 (milestones) and Level 2 (summary) to the client/operator; controlled at Level 3; expanded to Level 4–5 lookahead for roof-steel erection and commissioning — consistent with AACE 37R-06.
